newsitem.title: USA: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Call sellers in Microsoft, Morris.
newsitem.headline: US OPTIONS FOCUS/Call sellers in Microsoft, Morris.

text.p: Investors were busy selling calls in Microsoft Corp and Philip Morris Cos Inc, taking advantage of the two stocks' rallies, traders said Friday.
By about 1300 CDT/1800 GMT, Microsoft was up 8-1/8 at 106-1/4 on heavy turnover of more than 20.5 million shares.
The company reported higher than expected fiscal third quarter earnings on Thursday, and several brokerage firms raised full year estimates on Friday.
"There are a lot of call sellers today," said one trader in the Microsoft options trading crowd. "There's a heck of a lot of stock being bought.
"There isn't much interest in the puts," he said, adding that one of the popular strategies appeared to be buy-writing.
Buy-writing, also known as covered writing, occurs when an investor buys stock and sells call options simultaneously.
Among Microsoft options, the April 100 call was most active, with volume of about 8,135 contracts.
The option, which expires on Saturday, had open interest of 12,971 contracts. It was up 5-7/16 at 6-3/8.
Other busy Microsoft calls included the April 105, with volume of more than 7,500, the May 100, 105 and 110 calls and the July 110 call.
The most active Microsoft put was the April 105, which traded 3,530 contracts, followed by the May 100, which traded about 2,875.
The Microsoft options trader, at the Pacific Exchange, said most of the activity was coming from retail investors.
Gregory Nie, a technical analyst at EVEREN Securities in Chicago, said the stock has more upside potential.
"To me this looks like a breakout," Nie said of the stock's move. "The stock had outperformed its peers by holding the majority of its gains."
He explained that the stock broke down slightly recently when it fell below 94, but mitigated that breakdown on its recovery.

"If you're willing to wink a little bit at the one retreat down into the 80s (the stock fell to 87-1/2 intraday on March 24), it looks to me like you're looking at a move to 115 to 120, depending on how you push your pencil," Nie said.
He said that was an intermediate-term target.
Investors in Philip Morris calls were taking their profits as that stock rallied on institutional buying, traders said.
"The options are trading up a storm," said Andrew Schwarz, senior partner at AGS Specialist Partners in New York. "Most of the activity is closing April positions.
"They are on the call sell side," he said. "People who had bought the calls and are now selling out for profit."
He added that volatility in the Philip Morris options was holding relatively steady.
Trading was led by the April 43-3/8 and April 45 call, which traded about 8,655 and 6,940 contracts, respectively.
